papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Towards Imperceptible and Robust Adversarial Example Attacks against Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems based on deep neural networks, being able to produce state-of-the-art results on various perception tasks, have gained mainstream adoption in many applications. However, they are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial example attack, which generates malicious output by adding slight perturbations to the input. Previous adversarial example crafting methods, however, use simple metrics to evaluate the distances between the original examples and the adversarial ones, which could be easily detected by human eyes. In addition, these attacks are often not robust due to the inevitable noises and deviation in the physical world. In this work, we present a new adversarial example attack crafting method, which takes the human perceptual system into consideration and maximizes the noise tolerance of the crafted adversarial example. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

literature_themes.theme: Defending AI Models Against Data Poisoning Attacks
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on identifying and mitigating data poisoning attacks on AI models, particularly in the contexts of image recognition and recommendation systems. The studies propose various defense mechanisms, including novel detection algorithms, robust optimization strategies, and dual-defense frameworks that combine active and passive defenses to enhance model resilience and maintain performance. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of these approaches in reducing the impact of malicious data manipulation.
literature_themes.limitations: The cluster lacks comprehensive exploration of the long-term effectiveness of the proposed defenses in real-world scenarios. Additionally, the absence of an abstract for one paper limits the understanding of its contributions and findings. There is also a need for more diverse datasets and scenarios to validate the robustness of the proposed methods.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the critical need for advanced defense mechanisms against data poisoning, which is a significant research gap in AI security. By addressing vulnerabilities in various AI applications, the findings can guide future research towards developing more resilient AI systems.

literature_themes.theme: Adversarial Robustness in Deep Learning Applications
literature_themes.summary: This cluster focuses on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models against adversarial attacks, particularly in the contexts of neural networks and image super-resolution. It presents novel methods for crafting adversarial examples that are imperceptible to human perception and proposes techniques to mitigate the impact of adversarial noise in real-world image processing tasks.
literature_themes.limitations: The proposed methods may still face challenges in real-world applications due to the inherent variability of physical environments and the potential for new types of adversarial attacks that could circumvent the introduced defenses. Additionally, the balance between noise removal and image quality preservation remains a critical concern.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the need for further research into the development of more sophisticated adversarial defenses and the exploration of new metrics for evaluating adversarial robustness, thereby supporting the identification of gaps in current methodologies and prompting future investigations.

summary: The retrieved literature emphasizes the urgent need for robust AI systems capable of defending against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The first theme highlights various defense mechanisms against data poisoning, including dual-defense frameworks and robust optimization strategies, while the second theme focuses on enhancing adversarial robustness in deep learning applications through novel methods for crafting imperceptible attacks and mitigating adversarial noise. However, both themes reveal limitations in real-world applicability and the need for further research to develop comprehensive and adaptive defenses across diverse AI contexts.
scholarly_positioning: The existing literature on robust AI systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks reveals significant advancements in defense mechanisms, yet it remains fragmented and limited in scope. While prior approaches have introduced dual-defense frameworks and novel optimization strategies, they often lack comprehensive validation across diverse real-world scenarios, leaving critical vulnerabilities unaddressed. Furthermore, the focus on specific datasets and attack types raises concerns about the generalizability of these methods. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing adaptive and comprehensive defense strategies that not only enhance robustness against known threats but also anticipate emerging adversarial techniques, thus contributing to the broader discourse on AI security.
research_scope: This study will focus on developing adaptive and comprehensive defense strategies against data poisoning and adversarial attacks specifically in image recognition models. The target population will include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on diverse image datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the robustness of the proposed defense mechanisms will be assessed through experimental validation and ablation studies. A control group will consist of baseline models without the proposed defenses. Primary outcomes will include classification accuracy and resilience to various attack vectors, while secondary outcomes will measure the computational efficiency and generalizability of the defense strategies across different datasets and attack scenarios.

technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible as it primarily involves developing and testing defense strategies on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) using publicly available datasets like CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. It does not require hidden state extraction or open-source model access since the focus is on robustness evaluations and experimental validation of the models' outputs. However, it will require GPU resources for training and testing the models efficiently. The study does not involve human participants, thus no ethics approval is needed. A feasible adjustment could include ensuring access to sufficient computational resources for the experimental validation phase.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated various defense mechanisms against data poisoning attacks in AI models, particularly in image recognition contexts; however, they treat the long-term effectiveness of these defenses in real-world scenarios as secondary, leaving unclear whether the proposed methods maintain robustness against evolving attack strategies over time; this matters practically because the dynamic nature of adversarial threats necessitates ongoing resilience in AI systems; therefore, this study investigates the long-term effectiveness and adaptability of defense mechanisms against data poisoning in image recognition models within the defined scope.
question: How do adaptive defense mechanisms against data poisoning impact the long-term robustness and classification accuracy of convolutional neural networks trained on diverse image datasets compared to baseline models without these defenses?
theoretical_mechanism: In this research, the independent variable is the implementation of adaptive defense mechanisms against data poisoning. The mediator is the robustness of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as measured through classification accuracy and resilience to adversarial attacks. The moderator is the evolving nature of adversarial threats, which may impact the effectiveness of these defenses over time. The dependent variable is the long-term performance of CNNs on diverse image datasets. The theoretical framework is grounded in robustness theory, suggesting that enhanced defenses lead to improved system-level outcomes, such as reduced vulnerability to data poisoning, mediated by technical mechanisms like noise mitigation and feature extraction. User-level outcomes, such as user satisfaction with model performance, may be influenced by perceived reliability of the model, which is mediated by the model's sustained accuracy. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the stability of adversarial strategies and the adaptability of defense mechanisms over time.
hypothesis: Implementing adaptive defense mechanisms against data poisoning in convolutional neural networks will result in significantly higher long-term classification accuracy compared to baseline models without these defenses, mediated by increased robustness against evolving adversarial threats.

methodology: This study will develop and evaluate adaptive defense mechanisms against data poisoning in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) using CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets. The experimental design will include a control group of baseline CNN models without defenses, allowing for direct comparison of classification accuracy and robustness metrics. Adaptive defenses will be operationalized through the implementation of novel algorithms designed to enhance model resilience against evolving adversarial threats. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, resilience to various attack vectors, and computational efficiency, assessed at multiple intervals over a six-month period. To control for confounding variables, the study will ensure diverse dataset characteristics and systematically analyze different attack strategies. Reproducibility will be maintained by documenting the experimental setup and methodologies, while the scope will be limited to image recognition tasks to ensure focused insights into the effectiveness of the proposed defenses.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop adaptive and comprehensive defense strategies against data poisoning and adversarial attacks specifically in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) within the domain of machine learning method development. The study will focus on image recognition models trained on diverse datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, assessing the long-term effectiveness of these defenses through experimental validation and ablation studies over a six-month evaluation period. Key concepts include Robust AI Systems, defined as AI systems designed to maintain performance despite adversarial conditions, and Data Poisoning, a malicious attack where misleading data corrupts the learning process. The technical feasibility is supported by the use of publicly available datasets and the requirement for GPU resources for model training. Scholarly positioning reveals a fragmented landscape of existing literature, highlighting the need for comprehensive defenses that maintain robustness against evolving adversarial threats, particularly the lack of long-term effectiveness assessments of existing defense mechanisms. The central research question investigates how adaptive defense mechanisms against data poisoning impact the long-term robustness and classification accuracy of CNNs compared to baseline models without these defenses. The theoretical mechanism posits that enhanced defenses (independent variable) will improve CNN robustness (mediator), leading to better long-term performance (dependent variable), while the evolving nature of adversarial threats serves as a moderator. The falsifiable hypothesis states that implementing adaptive defense mechanisms will yield significantly higher long-term classification accuracy compared to baseline models, mediated by increased robustness against evolving adversarial threats. Construct operationalization includes metrics for adaptive defenses, CNN robustness, adversarial threats, and long-term performance, with classifications based on accuracy and resilience metrics. The methodology involves a control group of baseline models, ensuring diverse dataset characteristics, and systematic analysis of attack strategies. Expected contributions include a comprehensive framework for evaluating long-term defense effectiveness, novel adaptive algorithms, empirical findings on CNN performance, and practical deployment guidelines. Key limitations include potential confounding variables, the dynamic nature of adversarial threats, and the focus on specific datasets, which may affect generalizability.
